# Amos Chapter 8 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 336r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/AMO_008_page_001.jpg

---

**8:1** Thus the-Lord [Adonai] YHWH showed-me [hir'ani]: and-behold, a-basket [kelub] of-summer-fruit [qayits].

**8:2** And-he-said, "What [are] you seeing [ro'eh], Amos?" And-I-said, "A-basket of-summer-fruit [qayits]." And-said YHWH to-me, "The-end [ha-qets] has-come [ba] for-my-people Yisra'el; I-will-not again [lo osif od] pass-by [avor] for-him."

**8:4** Hear this, those-who-trample [ha-sho'afim] the-needy [evyon] and-bring-to-an-end [lehashbit] the-humble [aniyyei] of-the-land [arets],

**8:5** saying, "When will-the-new-moon [ha-chodesh] pass [ya'avor] and-we-will-sell [venashbirah] grain [shever], and-the-Sabbath [ha-shabbat] and-we-will-open [veniftechah] wheat [bar] — making-small [lehaqtin] the-ephah [eifah] and-making-great [u-lehagdil] the-shekel [sheqel] and-perverting [u-le'avvet] with-balances [moznei] of-deceit [mirmah]?"

**8:6** "To-buy [liqnot] the-poor [dallim] for-silver [ba-kesef] and-the-needy [evyon] for-a-pair of-sandals [na'alayim], and-the-refuse [mappal] of-wheat we-will-sell."

**8:11** "Behold, days [yamim] [are] coming [ba'im]," declares the-Lord YHWH, "and-I-will-send [vehishlachti] a-famine [ra'av] in-the-land — not a-famine of-bread [lechem] and-not a-thirst [tsama] for-water [mayim], but [ki im] of-hearing [lishmoa] the-words [divrei] of-YHWH."

**8:12** "And-they-will-stagger [vena'u] from-sea [mi-yam] to-sea [ad-yam], and-from-north [mi-tsafon] to-east [mizrach]; they-will-run-to-and-fro [yeshotetu] to-seek [levaqesh] the-word of-YHWH, and-they-will-not find [velo yimtse'u] [it]."


---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1-2 — The wordplay:** *Qayits* ("summer fruit") and *qets* ("end") — a devastating pun. The ripe fruit signals the end.

**v.5 — Rigged scales:** Merchants who can't wait for the Sabbath to end so they can resume cheating — shrinking the measure (*ephah*), inflating the price (*shekel*), rigging the balance. Amos exposes the intersection of false piety and economic fraud.

**v.11-12 — Famine of the word:** The most terrifying threat in the book — not physical famine but spiritual silence. YHWH will withdraw his word. The most devastating punishment is not destruction but divine silence.

*— EMET*
